answer:
**US dividends generally face 15% US withholding tax** when paid to an Irish-resident UCITS ETF entitled to US–Ireland treaty benefits, including satisfying the limitation-on-benefits test. This replaces the standard 30% rate.

The US withholding agent deducts the tax before the ETF receives the dividend. **The tax is incurred at fund level; ETF investors bear it economically** through lower investment returns—less income available for distribution or reinvestment. It is not a separate 15% withholding on payments from the ETF to its investors.

**Worth knowing:** Accumulating dividends does not avoid this withholding. Investors generally cannot personally reclaim or claim a foreign-tax credit for tax incurred by the ETF; their own local taxes are separate.
